title: Check: Volume of Pyramids and Cones

questions.stem: A cone and a cylinder have the same base radius and height. The volume of the cone is $50\text{ cm}^3$. What is the volume of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: A cone has $\frac{1}{3}$ the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height. If the cone is $50\text{ cm}^3$, the cylinder is $3 \times 50 = 150\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.stem: A pyramid has a volume of $96\text{ cm}^3$ and a rectangular base measuring $6\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$. What is its height?
questions.explanation: $V = \frac{1}{3} \times \text{base area} \times h$, so $96 = \frac{1}{3} \times 48 \times h = 16h$. Hence $h = 6\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: The general formula for the volume of a pyramid is:
questions.explanation: The volume of any pyramid (or cone) is $\frac{1}{3} \times \text{base area} \times \text{height}$.
